title: Technology Sector Update for 09/19/2018: IZEA,BABA,INTC,BIDU,SPLK

Technology stocks were moderately softer in Wednesday trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing nearly 0.2% in value, more than halving their prior decline, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has turned positive late this afternoon, rising over 0.3%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) IZEA ( IZEA ) was down almost 4% in late Wednesday trading after earlier pricing a $2.1 million public offering of more than 1.4 million shares of its common shares at $1.50 apiece, representing a 12% discount from Tuesday's closing price. The online marketing platform expects to use net proceeds to fund its growth strategy and for general working capital.
In other sector news:
(+) Alibaba ( BABA ) pushed out to a more than 4% gain on Wednesday after saying its cloud-services unit was partnering with chip-making giant Intel ( INTC ) on digital broadcasts from the upcoming 2020 summer Olympics in Tokyo. The companies expect to launch the cloud-based Olympic Broadcasting Services in two years using Intel's Xeon scalable processors while Alibaba will concentrate on a more efficient and reliable delivery of media from the XXXII Games to broadcasters worldwide.
(+) Baidu ( BIDU ) put up a more than 4% at one point on Wednesday after the Chinese technology company it was collaborating with Wabco Holdings ( WBC ) to develop braking control systems company for self-driving commercial vehicles. The companies expect to combine and adapt Baidu's Apollo autonomous driving software platform with Wabco's open source, self-driving platform to create advanced technologies for the commercial vehicle industry.
(-) Splunk (SPLK) dropped over 2% on Wednesday after the big-data analytics company overnight priced an upsized $1.85 billion private placement of its 0.50% convertible senior notes due 2023 and 1.125% convertible senior notes due 2025. The company placed $1.1 billion of the five-year convertible notes, up from its orginal plan to offer $850 million of the notes, while it trimmed the number of seven-year convertible notes it eventually sold by $100 million to $750 million. The company also said the initial conversion price for both the 2023 and 2025 notes will be $148.30 per share.
